#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <vector>

int main() {
    int n, b;
    scanf("%d %d", &n, &b);
    std::vector<int> arr1(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        scanf("%d", &arr1[i]);
    }

    // prefix sums for even (pf1) and odd (pf2) counts
    std::vector<int> pf1(n), pf2(n);
    int sum1 = 0, sum2 = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (arr1[i] % 2 == 0)
            ++sum1;
        else
            ++sum2;
        pf1[i] = sum1;
        pf2[i] = sum2;
    }

    int prev = 0; // note: prev is never updated in the original Java code
    std::vector<int> arr(n); // maximum possible size n
    int p = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n - 2; i += 2) {
        int x, y;
        if (prev == 0) {
            x = pf1[i];
            y = pf2[i];
        } else {
            x = pf1[i] - pf1[prev];
            y = pf2[i] - pf2[prev];
        }
        if (x == y) {
            arr[p] = std::abs(arr1[i + 1] - arr1[i]);
            ++p;
        }
    }

    // val array all 1
    std::vector<int> val(p, 1);
    // knapsack DP
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> K(p + 1, std::vector<int>(b + 1, 0));
    for (int i = 1; i <= p; ++i) {
        for (int w = 0; w <= b; ++w) {
            if (arr[i - 1] <= w)
                K[i][w] = std::max(val[i - 1] + K[i - 1][w - arr[i - 1]], K[i - 1][w]);
            else
                K[i][w] = K[i - 1][w];
        }
    }

    printf("%d\n", K[p][b]);

    return 0;
}
